title: This Is the Oldest Peace Treaty Ever Discovered - Nautilus
gist: Archaeologists found another fragment of the roughly 1269 BCE Egyptian-Hittite peace treaty at Büyükkale in Türkiye, containing articles 12 to 20, including rules on refugee treatment and a ban on destroying their homes.

insights.claim: The first known treaty between nations to cease hostilities dates to around 1269 BCE, between Pharaoh Ramses II of Egypt and Hittite King Hattusilli III, over disputed Syrian territories.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Historical anchor for how great-power conflicts over contested territory have long been settled by negotiated agreements.
insights.locator: The history of peace treaties goes back

insights.claim: Archaeologists have unearthed fragments of the treaty in the ruined Hittite capital over the last 120 years, and a new piece was just found.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Reminder that primary-source evidence is still being recovered.

themes.theme: Refugee provisions in the new fragment

insights.claim: The newly found piece from the Büyükkale site in Türkiye contains articles 12 through 20 and covers rules on refugee treatment, specifically that refugees' homes should not be destroyed.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Shows refugee protection was a bargaining item in interstate diplomacy over 3,000 years ago; useful framing for modern humanitarian norms.
insights.locator: Discovered in the rocky Büyükkale site
